dedupe_keys.name: nasa measures gfsad global crop dominance 2010 1 km gfsad1kcd v001

description: A global 1 km map of crop dominance for nominal 2010 from NASA's MEaSUREs Global Food Security Support Analysis Data (GFSAD) project. The NASA Earthdata page says it overlays the five dominant crops of the world from Ramankutty et al. (2008), Monfreda et al. (2008) and Portmann et al. (2009) on the IWMI remote sensing map of global irrigated and rainfed cropland, giving eight crop dominance classes, and that inputs included AVHRR, SPOT Vegetation and MODIS data, crop type data, elevation, 50-year precipitation and 20-year temperature, sub-metre to 5 m ground data and country statistics, from 2007 to 2012. The product, released in 2016 by the NASA Land Processes DAAC with Prasad Thenkabail and co-authors as creators, is openly shared under the EOSDIS data use guidance and free to download after an Earthdata login, with a user guide listing known issues. Coverage is global. Caveats: 1 km cells mix crops, the base year is about 2010, and later GFSAD 30 m products supersede it for cropland extent. For simulation it gives global crop type and irrigation class layers for exposure of crop production to drought, heat and floods. Related catalogue records include the USDA Cropland Data Layer and EarthStat.
